title: YouTube’s contextual AI search rolls out to all users on Android and iOS in US
key_facts: Google announced on 13 Oct 2026 that the "Ask YouTube" conversational AI search is rolling out widely to mobile users, in addition to TV instances of the YouTube app (9to5Google).
It is no longer limited to YouTube Premium subscribers and is accessible to all users.
It is powered by Gemini, so answers can go beyond what is in the video being watched.
Use from the watch page in the Shorts feed and during live streams will come in a later release.
For now users in the US can expect it on Android and iOS as it rolls out to more users; Google plans to expand availability gradually.
quote_evidence: Unlike before, Ask YouTube will now be accessible to all users, not just Premium subscribers.
It’s powered through Gemini, so its answers go beyond strictly what’s in the video you’re watching.
Google says it plans to gradually expand availability.
why_it_matters_hint: A conversational AI tool on the world's biggest video site moves from paid to free users on phones, in the US.
notes: Short article, no Google link quoted. The rollout is gradual and US only for now.
